notes: ACCESS: robots.txt (https://www.walmart.com/robots.txt) checked first - no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web disallow found, generic 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' list only covers /account/, /api/, cart/checkout paths, not category browse pages. Tier (a) direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi, impersonate=chrome120) was used for all data-bearing requests and worked reliably (200 OK, real __NEXT_DATA__/contentLayout JSON, no bot wall) for every one of the ~45 category pages fetched. A brief tier (b) Playwright (headless chromium) probe was also used: it worked fine for the general /cp/bedding/4044 'Home' hub page (used only for initial mega-menu discovery, no block), but hit a PerimeterX 'Robot or human?' challenge (blocked?url=...) when loading a specific /browse/ deep category page - that page was then successfully re-fetched via tier (a) curl_cffi instead, so no tier (c) Claude-in-Chrome escalation was needed; status is 'ok' not 'partial'. TREE: built as the union of (1) the site's full top-nav mega-menu, captured once via a single Playwright DOM link-extraction pass on the Home department hub page (492 links, filtered to ~90 Bedding/Bath/Decor/Storage&Organization/Kitchen&Dining candidates via each link's povid breadcrumb path e.g. HomeTopNav_BeddingBath_Bedding_DuvetCovers), and (2) each candidate category page's own contentLayout JSON (embedded in __NEXT_DATA__), which was walked recursively to recover further nested children not present in the top-nav (this is how Table Linens > Tablecloths/Placemats/Table Runners/Kitchen Linens/Outdoor Tablecloths and Shower Curtains > Liners/Extra Long/Standard/Sets were discovered). Every recorded leaf's own rendered <h1> text was checked to confirm it matches the requested node name (bad-slug/silent-wrong-number check) before being recorded. QTY: preferred order per rule was applied, but Walmart's rendered H1 caps every category above 1000 items at the literal text '(1000+)' (a genuine site-side display cap, not an estimate) - all rows showing this cap were recorded qty=null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than fabricating a number. Where the site displayed an exact number under the cap (Coverlets=3, Runner Rugs=508, Kids' Bath Rugs=282, Kids' Shower Curtains=517) that exact number was used. The GraphQL __NEXT_DATA__ 'aggregatedCount'/'totalItemCount' fields were checked as a possible exact-count source but rejected: two clearly different categories (Bath Towels vs Bed Sheets) returned the same suspiciously large aggregatedCount (179600-182676), proving this field reflects an inflated/shared value rather than the true per-category count (consistent with this project's 'storefront count APIs are inflated' precedent), so it was not used. EXCLUDED and why: Curtain Rods, Shower Curtain Rods, Shower Curtain Hooks & Rings - hardware, not textile (textile.md sec 5). Shower Curtain Liners, 'Extra Long'/'Standard' Shower Curtains, Shower Curtain Sets - facet/size/material variants nested inside the already-counted 'Shower Curtains' node (liners are typically vinyl/PEVA, not fabric); not recorded separately to avoid double counting the same listing. Rug Pads - a rug accessory/underlayment, not itself a floor textile. 'Blinds & Shades' hub - predominantly non-fabric venetian/wood/cellular blinds, no clearly-fabric Roman/Roller Blinds subcategory was found in its own contentLayout, so excluded. Decorative Bins & Baskets, Fabric Tablecloths, 5x7/8x10 Area Rugs - narrower style/size facets nested inside an already-counted broader sibling node, skipped to avoid double counting. Hangers - an organizing accessory, not itself a storage container (storage.md has no explicit hanger inclusion). Mason Jars & Canning Supplies, Shelf Liners, Trash Cans, Vacuum Sealers (Kitchen Storage siblings) - primary purpose is canning/food-prep/waste/surface-lining, not storage, excluded per the Kitchen & Dining boundary (storage.md sec 13/26). Coat Racks, Hall Trees - despite a 'StorageOrganization' povid tag in the mega menu, their actual URL path (4044_103150_...) places them under the Furniture department; excluded per the explicit website-hierarchy rule (storage.md sec 21/27), belongs to the separate Furniture task. Backpacks, Luggage & Travel, Kids Luggage, Weekenders & Duffels - personal-carrying travel bags, explicitly excluded (storage.md sec 6). The entire Garage/Home-Improvement storage cluster (Bike Racks, Garage Cabinets, Ceiling Storage, Heavy Duty Shelving, Metal Shelves, Shelving Units, Storage Systems, Tool Chests) sits under Walmart's separate 'Home Improvement' department (ID 1072864), not the 'Home' department (4044) the rest of this tree comes from - treated as out of Home/Living scope per the worker brief. The bad-slug facet URL '/browse/home/closet-organizers/4044_90828?facet=recommended_room:Closet' (department root + facet param, not a real category ID) was discarded in favor of the genuine ID-based 'Closet Organizers' node (.../4044_90828_1230061). SCOPE LIMITATION: no dedicated 'Shoe Storage/Shoe Racks' or 'Patio/Garden Storage' node was found within the Home department (4044) navigation surface actually crawled (top-nav mega menu + each visited page's own contentLayout children); shoe storage may exist inside the general Bins & Baskets/Storage Furniture listings without its own category URL, and outdoor/patio storage boxes may live under Walmart's separate Patio & Garden department which was not crawled (out of the mega-menu path captured from the Home hub). A second Playwright probe of the Storage & Organization hub page (cp/storage-organization/90828), attempted specifically to check for a shoe-storage child node, hit the same PerimeterX 'Robot or human?' wall seen earlier on a /browse/ page; per the stop-on-first-block rule this was not chased further since tier (a) curl_cffi already delivered a substantial, reliable tree and status remains 'ok'.
